version_guard.provenance: All four probes (scripts/probe-claude-contracts.sh, scripts/probe-stop-toolallowed.sh, scripts/probe-tui-second-turn.sh, scripts/probe-stop-edge-contracts.sh) ran against the concrete Claude Code 2.1.292 binary on 2026-10-07. Each probe stamped version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.292 end=2.1.292 with start == end == claude_version. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 12/12 event pairs with relay-first in 5/12; Arm D verified an errored Bash tool result in each of five denied runs and one Stop per run; Arm T killed all eight overrun firings while all four sessions exited 0 at the 5 s timeout. One authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 39-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The captured assistant tool-use record included wireToolInputs.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.292 Arm S: project hook sleeping 300 ms and relay hook 0 ms ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs; the relay started first in 5/12. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on which hook starts first.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.292 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 1.8 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with SECOND-OK rendered in 1.5 s. The allowed-tool probe completed one Stop per turn (30.5 s and 26.5 s); those timings are separate from the dedicated plain-turn probe.
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.292 used a command-specific Bash deny rule and verified an errored Bash tool result in each transcript. All 5 completed denied runs exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce. The poller keeps first-payload tolerance for degraded runs.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.292 permitted two sequential Bash rounds in one -p run and fired exactly 1 Stop at the completed turn end, exit 0. The independent max-turns probe exited 1 with 0 new Stop firings when --max-turns 2 cut off the four-round task.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.292 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and logged zero new Stop firings; the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.292 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s: all 8 event firings were killed, all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies rendered, and each Stop hook was cut off at 5.0 s. This confirms the per-hook timeout field used by the relay.
